item.description:
Using KeePassPasskey in a Corporate Environment

This guide is for IT administrators who want to roll out KeePassPasskey on managed Windows PCs, and for users who want to know what to ask their IT department for. For everyday use, see the User Guide; for individual problems, see FAQ & Troubleshooting.

Overview

KeePassPasskey consists of two parts, which are deployed separately:

Part What it is Where it lives
The app (KeePassPasskeyProvider.exe) An MSIX package that Windows activates as a passkey provider. It also hosts the KeePassPasskey app window Installed per user by Windows, like any MSIX app
The plugin (KeePassPasskey.dll) A KeePass plugin that creates and stores the passkeys and signs with them KeePass’s Plugins folder

Both must be present, and both must be on compatible versions (see Keeping the app and plugin versions matched).

FAQ & Troubleshooting

For end-user instructions and UI walkthroughs, see the User Guide.

Installation fails: the package is not compatible with the device

Error 0x80073CFD, “The package requires OS version 10.0.26100.0 or higher”, means your Windows is too old. KeePassPasskey needs Windows 11 24H2 or later (any edition), because the Windows passkey plugin API it is built on does not exist in Windows 10 or Windows 11 23H2.

Check your version with winver (Win + R). On 23H2, upgrade to 24H2 or later; Windows Update does not always offer this feature update right away, and on a work PC your IT department may need to roll it out.

User Guide

KeePassPasskey turns KeePass into a native Windows 11 passkey provider. Once installed, websites and apps that support passkeys will offer KeePassPasskey as a storage option, and passkeys are saved directly into your KeePass database.

Requirements

  • KeePass 2.54 or later
  • Windows 11 24H2 or later, with TPM* enabled and Windows Hello* set up

Installation

See the installation instructions in the README for the full setup steps. After installation, both status indicators in the KeePassPasskey app should show green. You can open the app at any time from the Start menu by searching for “KeePassPasskey” to check or adjust the configuration, or for debugging purposes. You do not need to keep it open: the passkey provider runs as a Windows integration in the background and is activated by Windows whenever a passkey operation is requested.
